business_problem: Polimill needed to reduce administrative burden across fragmented Japanese municipal systems so public employees could find prior decisions, prepare assembly responses, and deliver services without each municipality building separate AI tools.
solution_summary: Polimill built QommonsAI as a shared generative AI foundation for municipal work in Japan. The platform started by standardizing assembly minutes and other administrative records that were previously scattered across municipalities, then applied AI to add metadata and create a searchable cross-municipality knowledge base. QommonsAI now supports workflows such as assembly response, public services, social welfare, and legal search for about 1,050 municipalities and roughly 550,000 public employees. OpenAI GPT models provide the reasoning layer, while QommonsAI adds public-sector controls so administrators can inspect feature-usage history and restrict model availability according to policy. Polimill also uses Codex across its own development lifecycle—from requirements and code-consistency checks to implementation and testing—which accelerated validation cycles with municipal users and helped the company evolve the system toward a broader public OS and future super-agent marketplace called Qommons ONE.

Public-sector workers query that shared knowledge base through GPT-powered interfaces, while Polimill’s internal team uses Codex to rapidly build and refine the platform from municipal feedback.
